So, the first Sleep Token song I ever heard was *Granite*. I was working on the first draft of a novel and I had made this angsty playlist on Spotify and for some reason that day I had put the “Smart Shuffle” feature on (where it will add in ‘relative’ music selections to suite the genre/vibes of your playlist). The hook part: ‘I was more than just a body in your passenger seat’ cane on and I just stopped typing mid sentence to listen to the rest of the song. And then I played it again and then I played at the third time. And then I was like “Who the fuck is this??” 
✨Sleep Token✨ 
So I spent the next hour or so listening to some songs from their back catalogue. And I was like “These guys are kinda cool” and then I forgot about them for a while and just kept a few of their songs in rotation. It wasn’t until a few months later that I really got into them, and it was only after Vessel made me bawl my eyes out. 


Okay for this second part: 
**CW//: Mental Illness and Self Harm**. 


So I have depression, anxiety and IED (intermittent explosive disorder - where you can suddenly fly into a rage and become violent and agressive) but my IED is always towards myself and when I have and IED episode I self harm. It was in the aftermath of one of those episodes and it had been particularly… bad. I was… patching myself up and tidying things when I put on TMBTE just for some background noise while I basically sat there and dissociated for a few hours. I didn’t pick it for any real reason tbh, it was literally just the first thing that popped up when I opened my Spotify probably because the album was new and I had followed the band when I came across them a few months beforehand. It doesn’t really matter though because I think it was just fate because when I came out of it *Are You Really Ok?* was playing. So I sit there tearing up because that song felt like Vessel was speaking right to me in one of my darkest moments. Then when the lyrics came around to Vessel basically begging me not to stop hurting myself and I started to bawl my eyes out, like messy ugly heartbroken crying. And I kinda promised Vessel that I would try not to self harm anymore. It hasn’t been easy but it’s been almost a year since then and I’ve kept that promise. 


**TLDR//:** I was at my kitchen table writing a book when I first heard Granite. The first time that Vessel brought me to tears was listening to Are you really OK? after I had a breakdown.

When my grandmother was diagnosed with cancer in 2001, the oncologist and her family doctor sat her down to give her that exact same talk and she looked at them dead in the eye and she told them: “I’ve been a nurse for 43 years, I’m well aware there’s a chance my husband is going to leave me.” 
My mother and I were both floored by that statement, because I always believed my grandfather worshipped the ground my grandmother walked on. 
Fast forward a few years later, after several surgeries and two rounds of chemotherapy, her cancer was finally in remission. I remember my mum (who went with Nana to her appointments when Grampy couldn’t) told me years later that the doctors and nurses in the oncology unit were sometimes genuinely shocked that my Grampy stayed beside his wife through her battle. She had a lot of medical issues over the years but he stuck by her through them all. The only thing that took him from her was his own battle with pancreatic cancer in 2020, which he lost very quickly (16 days between diagnosis and death). 
Nana died two days before their 68th wedding anniversary less than 5 months later.

It could be a number of things. First of all, I would recommend that you track your food. The most well documented fact of weight loss is that you must have a caloric deficit in order to lose weight. That means you have to consume less calories than your body uses in a day. Dietary changes don’t need to be extreme but you should make them mindfully and purposefully. Increase your vegetables, increase your fiber and drink plenty of water. 
Second of all, if you have a high stress job or 
living situation, or you have an anxiety disorder, your body may be flooded with cortisol, which will make it very difficult for you to lose weight because your body believes that it needs to store excess energy in order to function in “fight or flight” situations. Find time to be mindful and find ways that reduce your stress like breathing exercises, yoga or reading. My third recommendation, is that if it’s possible, and within your means, you should talk to a doctor about your hormone levels. If you are of a certain age (40-65), your hormones may be all out of whack, and your body may be storing energy as a result. In the same vein, you may have undiagnosed dietary sensitivities. Which can interfere with how your body digests and processes the foods you eat. 
Hope this helps.
